# SECTION - G # Door-Step Banking for Senior Citizens and Differently-Abled ## Introduction Reserve Bank of India advised Banks to have a scheme for providing services on the doorstep of its customers with the approval of the Board. This document enumerates a comprehensive policy setting up a framework within which the Doorstep Banking services would be provided to the customer. RBI guidelines on Doorstep Banking were issued in 1993, 2005, 2007 and 2017. This policy documents takes references from these circulars as a guided reference. ## Definition The term “Door Step Banking" shall include the following services: Pick up of cash for deposit into own accounts. Pick up of instrument (cheques / Remittance forms) for credit to own account. Delivery of cash by withdrawal from own accounts. Delivery of Demand draft and pay order issued by debit to own account. Submission of KYC document by Senior citizen (Citizens aged over 60 years) and differently-abled Any other service which RBI guides from time to time. ## Customer The term customer will be defined as a resident account holder maintains a savings or a current account with Unity Bank. The door step banking service will be offered only on working days of a branch to those customers who satisfy the following conditions. The list of branches where the services are offered shall be displayed on the website of the Bank. Single account holders and Joint Account Holders with Either or Survivor/ Former or Survivor All the KYC document in procession of the bank are in current and there are no deferrals pending on account of documentation The account is operative in nature Inoperative account holders can activate the door step banking after activating the account post submission of the necessary documents. All relevant application / forms are signed by the customer for availing such facility. INTERNAL Version 4.0 Master Policy on Customer Service ## Operating guidelines

The Door step banking service can be offered by the bank through any of the following means. By Banks own regular staff Outsourcing the operations to a Cash management vendor who have national / regional presence with a good track record. The outsourcing to such vendor will be governed by the outsourcing policy of the bank. Through banking correspondents empaneled with the bank. Services provided through outsourcing or through banking correspondents will be through a mutually signed agreement detailing the terms and conditions including charges for executing these services, turnaround time. ## Process of service delivery The service request for Door-Step delivery can be received at the branch or through any secure convenient channel like phone banking, IVR, Internet Banking, Mobile Banking or call center where the requests are authenticated using TPIN or any other acceptable authentication methodology. The service will be offered across all the branches of Unity Bank • These services will be rendered to the customer by the bank ONLY at customer's premises or residence, as per the address registered with the Bank Requests made through branches before 11:00 a.m. will be attended on the same day. Requests made post 11:00 a.m. will be attended on the next working day The limits of cash pickup and delivery will be decided by bank from time to time. This may vary from type of account held to different variant within a single type of accounts. A representative grid but which are subject to change on the limits on cash delivery / pickup are detailed below. # Cash collected from the customer will be issued an acknowledgement by way of receipts / Registered (Mobile no's) SMS / Registered e – mail. For instruments like cheques the customers will be informed about the probable date of credit into the account through suitable means like SMS (To registered mobile no.) Email id (registered with the bank). Use of technology is encouraged to credit / debit the customer on real time basis. The bank will make true efforts (On Best effort basis) to complete the request on the day of on-boarding of the request before 11 a.m. However, in scenarios where the bank is unable to complete the request on the same day in spite of receiving the instruction before 11 a.m., the customer will be informed accordingly, to avoid further inconvenience. Version 4.0 Master Policy on Customer Service INTERNAL ## Service Charges Service charges for door step banking if any will be levied on customers account basis a preagreed schedule of charges communicated through an official communication / brochures / schedule of charges / web site etc. The Bank may decide to charge the customer differentially basis the cost it incurs in delivering such services or by different variant of account or by size of the relationship with the bank. Any change in the service charges will be intimated to customers through any of the modes o Websites o Mobile banking alerts o Notice Boards o SMS / email to registered email id or registered mobile numbers The Bank shall inform at least 1 month in advance of any change to the schedule of charges on account of door step banking services. ## Force Majeure The Bank shall not be liable to compensate customers for delayed credit or delayed delivery / nondelivery of services for reasons beyond the control of the Bank [including but not limited to civil commotion, sabotage, lockout, strike or other labour disturbances, accident, fires, natural disasters or other “Acts of God", war, damage to the bank's facilities or of its correspondent bank(s), absence of the usual means of communication or all types of transportation, etc.] that prevent the bank from performing its obligations within specified service delivery parameters. ## Section 1: Know Your customer process

## 1.1 Account Opening – Retail Accounts
Individuals can open an account in a single name or in joint capacity. Joint holders will be family members / close relatives. A joint account can be opened with nonrelatives in an exceptionally rare case subject to approval from Cluster Heads, which should be handled with caution. Savings / Term Deposit Accounts of a Minor up to the age of 10 years or more can be opened by a natural guardian (including mother as guardian) or otherwise by a guardian appointed by a Court of Law or by Testamentary guardian (Guardian appointed through probated will). In such cases, a probate of the will should be obtained from the claimants.
Minors above such an age limit not less than 10 years (who are literate) and up to such amount and such terms as may be fixed by the banks keeping in view their risk management policy, may be allowed to open and operate savings/ term deposit accounts independently, if they so desire, and such terms shall be duly conveyed to the account holder. In such accounts, nomination form should be signed by the guardian.

A. When a customer approaches the bank for opening an account, a general interview/customer due diligence is conducted by Bank official (RM) to understand the need of the customer and accordingly account opening form, Personal Information Sheet (PIS), KYC Documents and recent photograph. FATCA form is incorporated in the PIS form wherein account holders must declare their tax residency status. If customer is declaring Multi-Tax Residency or Non-Resident of India, separate FATCA Form is to be obtained from customer with proper TIN Number and other details. Details of KYC documents to be obtained which is acceptable for Customer Identification are as below.
The documents obtained should be verified with original -
a. Any one Officially Valid Documents (OVD) - the passport, the driving license, proof of possession of Aadhaar number, the Voter's Identity Card issued by the Election Commission of India, job card issued by NREGA duly signed by an officer of the State Government and letter issued by the National Population Register containing details of name and address.

## Account opening of illiterate person:
The rules relating to Savings Bank or other deposit account must be clearly explained to an illiterate person intending to open such accounts in a language in which he/she understands. He / she shall be advised that for withdrawing money from his/her account, he/she must personally come to the Bank with the Passbook, every time.
It is advised that Left thumb impression in case of a male person, and right thumb impression in case of a female person of the constituent has to be obtained on the Account Opening Form in the presence of an authorized Bank officer and a person well known to the Bank who shall attest his thumb impression on the Account Opening Form as witness along with the witness details.(Name ,address, a/c no, etc)
Bank official who is obtaining thumb impression shall affix his/her signature near the thumb impression and add the words “Left/Right hand thumb impression of Mr./Mrs./MS”.
A declaration shall be taken from the illiterate depositor on the account opening form to the effect that the contents of account opening form as also the rules governing the deposit account have been explained to him, that he / she has fully understood the rules and that he had affixed his thumb impression after fully knowing the rules. This declaration shall be authenticated by the depositor by affixing his thumb impression and it shall be countersigned by a witness.

INTERNAL
In The case of an illiterate person, it shall be prominently written on account opening form that the account is of an “illiterate person”.
Photograph and thumb impression of the person shall be scanned and stored in the CBS system to verify the identity
The Pass Books of such customers should invariably have photographs, attested by the bank, pasted in the inner front page or the space provided in the passbook for the purpose.
Cheque Book shall not be issued to him under any circumstances and third-party cash withdrawal cannot be made.
Usually, no joint account of illiterate with literate person are opened by the Bank as illiterates are gullible and are prone to cheating by the literate. However, it may be allowed in case of joint account between close relatives with genuine request, but adequate safeguard shall be taken to avoid any inappropriate use. Such account shall be opened with the condition that both can only jointly operate it. No cheque book shall be issued even for such joint accounts.
During the operations in the accounts whenever the passing officer or authorized official notices a visible change in the resemblance of the photograph with the customer, particularly in the case of illiterate customers, a recent photograph shall be obtained from the customer, duly attested and affixed at all appropriate places. In such case, fresh AOF should be obtained from the customer where the latest photograph should be affixed and thereafter filed with the earlier AOF submitted by the customer.
Payment shall be made in the presence of one witness who is preferably a close relative. Signature and name of the witness shall be obtained on the withdrawal slip.

## 1.8 Account portability or Home Branch Change
The home branch of a bank account holder is the branch where the account is initially opened and the process of knowing your customer (KYC) is completed. The relevance of the home branch has decreased with banks providing online facilities and at par cheques to account holders.
However, banks provide facility to get the account transferred from one branch to another branch I.e the customer can opt for changing his/her home branch.

## 1.8.1 Scenario in which the home branch is changed.
• Change /Shifting of residence/business/workplace of the customer.
• The proximity of the branch is near to the workplace of the customer.
• There is a new branch of the bank which is nearer than the existing branch of the account holder.
• Business parked at other branches.
For e.g., business generated during marketing before launch of the branch is parked in any of the existing branches and after launch of the branch, such accounts and fds to be transferred to the new branch.
#UNITY Small Finance Bank
Unity Small Finance Bank Ltd.
INTERNAL
• The exact name of the new branch where the account is to be transferred.

## 1.8.2 Process for Branch change.
➢ For Branch Change activity, Branches to collect the application and documents from customer and send the request to Centralised Processing Team via CRM application for further CBS changes.
➢ A written request can be submitted to the branch where the customer wants to shift the account. The request letter has to be signed by all the account holders and the same has to be verified by the branch official. However, if the customer submits the letter in his/her own format, then the same can be accepted.

## ➢ The customer can request for branch change through registered email id only in below cases:
• If the account is held by the customer singly.
• If there is no change of address of the customer.
• In such cases the branch would make a call back to the customer at the registered phone number and reconfirm the instructions are sent by the customer, and same shall be noted on the request form with date, time, and signing by the branch official.

## ➢ The request letter/mail should clearly state the following:
• reason for changing the home branch.
• clearly indicate the account number/s which are to be transferred to another branch.

## Procedure to be followed by the branches:
• Obtain request letter from the account holder. The letter should be in warded, and the signature of the customer (all account holders) should be verified as per our records.
New account opening form is not required to be obtained, unless there is any addition or deletion of names, but branches should check for account opening form and KYC documents in AOF is dully filled and complete in all respect including details of nomination.
• KYC once done by one branch of the Bank will be valid for transfer of the account within the Bank as long as full KYC has been done for the concerned account.
• If KYC updation is due, then Data updation form to be obtained along with latest KYC documents.
• Form DA 3 to be obtained if the customer requests for change of nomination
• Also ensure that the PIS is obtained with income details and said details are updated in the customer master.
The account opening form should have all KYC documents including PAN/ FORM 60, OVD and FATCA application etc. which should be updated in the customer master as well as scanned copies should be uploaded in BIDMS. If any of the documents are not available, the home branch should be requested to upload said documents immediately for checking the same.
Ensure that the latest address and contact details including latest mobile number & email ids are obtained & updated in customer master. In case of change in address, the latest address with the address proof should be obtained & updated in CRM as well as scanned copies of same to be uploaded in BIDMS.
• Check the status of the account whether the account is active or Inoperative. If the account is Inoperative, initiate necessary process for activation of the account followed by customer induced transaction as SOL change of active account can be done.
• If the account is already lien noted or freeze marked then ensure that the said lien or freeze is continued after porting of an account.
The existing cheque book should be obtained by the branch and destroyed & new cheque book should be issued to the customer after transfer of account to the other branch, which will hold the revised MICR code.
• Post completion of documentation, branches shall send the application along with documents to CPC Team for further changes in CBS.

## 1.10 Closure of accounts

## A) Reasons for closure of bank account
The Bank Account of the customer may be closed for various reasons which are as follows:
1) The customer himself would like to close the account due to various reasons like shifting of residence, transfer of service/job to such a place where there are no bank’s branches
2) On account of death of the customer, the account of the customer has to be closed.
3) The bank can forcibly close the account,
a) if the account is inactive/inoperative without any balance for the long time
b) the bank has suspected /notices funds from illegal/fraudulent activity is routed through the account.
c) If the customer is found in negative list during screening
d) If the customer fails to comply the KYC of the account
e) If there is frequent Inward cheque return in the account

## B) Procedure for closure of account:
When the customer himself would like to close the account due to various reason like shifting of residence, bad experience with the staff, locality of the branch, etc
1) Just as the account is opened with the consent of both, it can be closed only with the consent of both. All the account holders should be physically present for giving their consent to close the account.
2) A written application signed by all the account holders should be obtained.
3) On accepting the application branch staff first needs to check

e. Funds pending in Amalgamation.

16) Account closure request can be submitted by customer at another branch and forward the request to home branch. Home branch will handle account closure process.

## A) Mandate:
A mandate is a simple letter of authority, signed by a constituent authorizing the bank to permit a certain named person to operate the account on his/her behalf. One can appoint a mandate holder by submitting a mandate form along with the requisite documents to the bank to allow a certain individual to operate his account. Thus, a mandate is given for allowing somebody to operate the account, to make, draw, accept or otherwise sign bills of exchange & other negotiable instruments or sometimes, even to overdraw the account.
• Mandates are very often used by the Current Account Holders.
Operations in accounts includes All type of remittances (Transfers/NEFT/RTGS, Issue of Demand Drafts/Pay orders, Inward clearing cheques, Cash withdrawals/deposits) are allowed to be done by Authorized Signatories.
• Branches to follow below guidelines for Appointment of mandate holder in customer’s account:
➢ A mandate is a simple letter of authority where stamping is not required.
➢ Operating instructions must be clearly mentioned in the Mandate form.
➢ KYC documents as per the Master Direction - Know Your Customer (KYC) Directions, 2016 i.e. Photo, OVD (Officially Valid Document), ID, Address proof and FATCA declaration and Personal Information Sheet of the Authorized Signatory should be obtained.
➢ Signature of the Mandate Holder should be obtained on Mandate form and also in the Account Opening Form along with rubber stamp as “Authorized Signatory”/ “Mandate Holder”.
➢ New CIF to be created for mandate holder if does not exist.
➢ CIF to be added in Authorized Signatory tab at Account Level in CBS and remarks to be added as “Mandate holder appointed with effect from”Date”
➢ Mode of operation to changed in CBS as per instruction.
➢ Signature of Mandate holder to be scanned.

## Revocation of the Mandate

Unity Small Finance Bank Ltd.
INTERNAL
• The mandate will be in force till the customer (Executant) informs the Bank in writing, that he has revoked the same. Mandate can be revoked or would stand revoked if the executant dies.
• The mandate shall stand automatically cancelled / extinguished under law, in the event of the death, insolvency or insanity of the customer (Executant).

## B) Letter of Authority:
Letter of Authority is a document under which one person authorises another person to do a particular act. Hence it is used for very specific purpose. A Letter of Authority (LOA) is a legal document that authorises a third party to correspond with service providers on behalf of person and his/her business. An LOA may or may not identify how an action is to be carried out. LOAs are typically used for more specific, administrative tasks. LOAs are typically simpler and may not need to specify the exact manner in which the task is to be performed.
e.g. LOA can be used for collecting or submitting documents on behalf of a person, LOAs are more commonly used for tasks like submitting documents, making inquiries, or managing routine administrative duties.
In case if a third party is visiting the branch for any service on behalf of customer on a regular basis then one- time Authority Letter can be obtained even if the third party is a family member.
1. To get the Principal (customer) to attest the signature of the Agent (mandate holder) on the Mandate letter / LOA document.
2. To include a clause in the Mandate letter / POA / LOA that the said instructions shall remain valid and in force unless the same is revoked in writing and communicated to the Bank by the principal (customer).
Branches to follow below guidelines for Appointment of mandate holder in customer’s account:
➢ Verify the content in the LOA
➢ Verify signature of the customer with bank records.
➢ The Branch would do a call back to the customer at the registered phone number and reconfirm that the instructions has been sent by the customer and same shall be noted on the request form with date, time and sign by Branch Official.
➢ The staff member calling back the customer will send an email to the registered email address of the customer confirming the discussion.
➢ ID card of the third party to be obtained.

## C) Power of Attorney:

When large & proper transactions are to be carried out, one should opt for a Power of Attorney & to appoint a Grantee through a POA, the documents must be signed before a public notary and stamped with appropriate stamp duty.
i) Applicable as per respective State Stamp Act.
ii) If the POA is to be used in States other than the home state, then the stamping has to done for the highest of the stamp duty applicable to POAs across the respective States involved.
A POA can be of two types--- General & Special power of attorney.
1. Special POA-- If the appointment is made for a specified act or acts.
2. General POA—If the appointment is made generally for certain acts.
LOA usually conveys a relation of master & servant, whereas the attorney relation is more like a principal & agent.
Task specified under the letter of authority is usually done under the ‘direct’ control & supervision of the person bestowing the authority whereas in the case of power of attorney, there is a greater scope for independence.
POAs grant broader and potentially more complex authority, allowing the agent to make significant decisions.
POAs can involve detailed instructions and limitations on the agent's powers.
POAs are often used in situations where the principal is unable to act on their own, such as due to incapacitation or travel.
While acting on POA, nothing should be assumed. Power to operate account does not give authority to open/close and transfer the account and deal with negotiable instruments. Power to operate account does not give power to overdraw.
1. If specifically provided for in the POA, attorney may sign cheques on behalf of the principal clearly indicating that he/she is acting on behalf of the principal. E.g. -
For Mr. XYZ
Constituted Attorney
OR
For Mr. XYZ
POA Holder
2. POA Holder may give instructions to Bank to STOP PAYMENT of cheques issued from the account; however, POA holder does not have the powers to revoke the stop-payment instructions.
That prerogative belongs only to account holder.
3. POA holder does not have the power to freeze / unfreeze operations in an account. That prerogative belongs only to account holder.

The Branches should be careful in accepting the POA. The POA should be current in nature. The Branches should periodically say, once in a year, confirm that the POA is still in force and it is not revoked, and the customer is alive. \*\*
1. Also to ensure that the POA does not contain onerous clauses which may be operationally difficult for the Bank to comply with.
2. Also ensure that POA does not contain conditional clauses that might introduce uncertainty; the POA should clearly and definitively grant the attorney the authority to act on the principal's behalf. Branches to follow below guidelines for Appointment of POA holder in customer’s account:

• Power of Attorney bears a Notarial Number as per the Register of the Notary.

The Power of Attorney can be revoked or would stand revoked if the executant dies or becomes of unsound mind or the executant is adjudged insolvent or on liquidation of the Company.
